scores.claim_text: The F-35, our largest S&D program, represents <25% of S&D revenue; sales dependent upon government funding.
scores.interpretation: F-35 RDT&E (Continuous Capability Development & Delivery) is funded steady at $1.24B FY24 and F-35 Squadrons operational-systems development at $89M FY24. Program-of-record health is intact at cutoff. Hexcel's claim that F-35 is its single largest S&D program (<25% of $544.8M = at most ~$136M, ~7.6% of total HXL sales) is structurally supported — the program is the largest tactical-aircraft procurement in DoD (production line not in J-Book RDT&E corpus but is documented continuing). No divergence. PASS.

scores.claim_text: CH-53K (King Stallion) is a future growth program for Hexcel composites (blades + airframe).
scores.interpretation: Navy/USMC aviation procurement program; not present in the ~410-program corpus (heavy AF RDT&E weighting + selected procurement). Per heuristic #7, NOT_FOUND is treated as UNVERIFIABLE (coverage gap, not red flag). Coverage gap noted: extend corpus with Navy Aircraft Procurement (1506 line items) to confirm. Outside corpus, public Navy P-40s through cutoff date document CH-53K as a multi-year program of record.

scores.claim_text: UH-60 (Black Hawk) wide-chord blade program is one of Hexcel's two largest blade programs.
scores.interpretation: Army Aircraft Procurement line (Sikorsky multi-year contract). The J-Book corpus does not include Army Aircraft Procurement P-40s for UH-60M. Heuristic #7 applies: NOT_FOUND → UNVERIFIABLE. Coverage gap. Independent context: Army FY24 budget continues UH-60M multi-year VIII procurement, but this is not confirmed in our corpus.

scores.claim_text: V-22 (Osprey) blades are one of Hexcel's two largest blade programs.
scores.interpretation: The corpus only contains CV-22 RDT&E ($16.6M FY24); V-22 production line items not in corpus. At cutoff this returns FUNDED_STEADY. HOWEVER, the V-22 multi-year procurement was already publicly winding down by 2024 (Navy/USMC announcing end of V-22 production around this period). The RDT&E line is small and shrinks materially in out-years (FY26 = $0.65M visible in raw program record though outside cutoff). Hexcel says V-22 blades are one of its top-2 blade programs as of FY23/22 — i.e., past revenue real, but forward V-22 procurement narrative is structurally weakening. Score MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY because materiality test (heuristic #2) treats this as Hexcel's claim of being a top-2 blade program (existential to blades sub-business), and CV-22 RDT&E small + production sundown. Caveat: production line not in corpus, so partial coverage limits severity escalation.

scores.claim_text: Hexcel is qualified to supply the Airbus A400M military transport.
scores.interpretation: A400M is a multi-national European program (Airbus DS / OCCAR) not funded out of US DoD J-Book. By design outside corpus scope. UNVERIFIABLE — not a red flag. To verify, would need EU defense budget data (not in pentagon_jbook source).

scores.claim_text: Space products: solid rocket booster cases, fairings, satellite bus, solar arrays — military + commercial launch and satellites; Space & Defense growth supported by space programs globally.
scores.interpretation: Hexcel does not appear as a primary J-Book contractor on any specific space PE (expected: tier-2/3 composite supplier to launch primes like Northrop Grumman, RTX, ULA, SpaceX). Claim is generic (no PE named, no revenue %). STP funded steady at cutoff. Per heuristic #2 — materiality test — the claim is not pinned to any named PE so no specific divergence test is possible. Treated as PASS (claim is descriptive of broad market, not load-bearing on a specific PE).

scores.claim_text: Space & Defense market = 30% of FY23 net sales ($544.8M), up 17.1% YoY; demand driven by US + Western European military aircraft procurement.

M_value.note: Direct DoD prime awards to Hexcel + ARC Technologies are de minimis vs $544.8M S&D revenue — consistent with tier-2/3 supplier model where revenue flows through primes (Lockheed/Sikorsky/Boeing/Bell-Boeing).

scores.interpretation: Direct prime contracts to Hexcel = ~$8.6M total cumulative — three orders of magnitude smaller than reported $544.8M S&D revenue. This is INTERNALLY CONSISTENT with Hexcel's disclosed business model (composites supplier to primes, not a prime contractor). No divergence. PASS.

scores.claim_text: 39% of 2023 net sales were to Airbus and its subcontractors (35% Commercial, 4% S&D).
scores.interpretation: Commercial customer-concentration disclosure; not a J-Book-testable claim. Counterparty disclosure (Airbus) would require Airbus 20-F / commercial-aerospace cross-check outside the J-Book framework. UNVERIFIABLE under this cohort's primary verifier; non-J-Book control claim as designed.

scores.claim_text: 15% of 2023 net sales were to Boeing and its subcontractors.
scores.interpretation: Boeing's EDGAR filings through cutoff do not name 'Hexcel' in full-text — standard behavior for primes who rarely name tier-2 material suppliers in 10-K body. Absence of counterparty mention is not contradictory. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: New carbon fiber line in Decatur, AL resumed in 2023; expected aerospace-qualified late 2025 / early 2026.
scores.M_check: no_jbook_pe_named; facility/capex claim outside cohort scope
scores.interpretation: Capacity-build claim; not a J-Book-testable program-revenue assertion. Non-J-Book control claim. UNVERIFIABLE under this cohort's primary verifier.

framework_notes: HXL is a tier-2 composites supplier with diffused program exposure (F-35 largest <25% of S&D, no other >10%). The J-Book divergence pattern (small-cap pinning >50% revenue to one zeroed PE) does not apply structurally to HXL.
Largest J-Book PE Hexcel names (F-35 RDT&E + F-35 Squadrons) is FUNDED_STEADY at cutoff — no PASS-to-RED flip.
Primary risk surfaced: V-22 (CV-22 RDT&E small + declining out-years even pre-cutoff). MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY for the V-22 blade-program claim, since V-22 was a top-2 blade program for HXL.

Coverage gaps in corpus: CH-53K (USN/USMC procurement), UH-60 (Army Aircraft Procurement), A400M (European Airbus DS) — all material to HXL but outside corpus scope. Treated as UNVERIFIABLE per heuristic #7, not red flags.
Commercial Aerospace (60% of revenue, Airbus A350 + Boeing 787 drivers) is the dominant revenue driver — outside J-Book entirely. This cohort's primary verifier has limited reach for HXL.
